examples: amarillo: Check plans against 2021 IRC (excluding Part VIII Electrical; Appendices A-J adopted) (city adoption) and energy code 2015 IECC last confirmed; 2021-cycle update not confirmed instead of the plain 2021 IRC model

arlington: Check plans against 2021 IRC (Arlington local amendments, Construction Chapter Art. I Sec. 1.04) (city adoption) and energy code 2021 IECC (Arlington amended, adopted 11-1-2022) instead of the plain 2021 IRC model
austin: Use 2024 IRC (not 2021) as base residential code for Austin permits applied on/after 2025-07-10
beaumont: Check plans against 2021 IRC (city adoption) and energy code 2021 IECC instead of the plain 2021 IRC model
amarillo: Use climate zone 4B envelope tables (higher wall/ceiling R, lower fenestration U than CZ 3); energy edition unconfirmed (2015 IECC last confirmed)
arlington: Apply 2021 IECC Climate Zone 3A envelope tables.
austin: Use 2024 IECC CZ 2A envelope with Austin amendments (not state 2021 IECC)
beaumont: Use climate zone 2A envelope tables; state floor is 2015 IRC Ch. 11 (ERI option under HSC 388.003)
arlington: RS-7.2: front 20 ft (40 ft on arterial/collector), street side 15 ft, interior side 5 ft (assumed), rear 20 ft; plat lines govern.
austin: SF-3/SF-2 setbacks: front 25, interior side 5, street side 15, rear 10 ft
beaumont: Default RS Residential Single-Family Dwelling (assumed): front 25, side 5, street side 10, rear 25 ft - ASSUMED, require user to confirm from plat/zoning letter
brownsville: R-1: front 25 / corner street side 20 / side 5 / rear 5 ft (side/rear from third-party; verify)
arlington: Flag an engineered (PE-sealed) post-tensioned slab as the default for expansive DFW clay; confirm whether the city amendment mandates it.
beaumont: Flag engineer-designed slab for expansive clay
brownsville: Flag engineered slab (expansive Rio Grande delta clays) - assumed
cedar-park: Flag PE-sealed engineered slab (expansive clay east of I-35 / variable limestone and clay in the west)
arlington: Add water $828 + sewer $418 per 5/8 meter, plus roadway $253-312.50 per vehicle-mile by service area.
austin: Add Austin Water impact fees $4,800 water + $2,900 wastewater per unit (lots platted after 2023-10-01)
brownsville: Add city capital recovery fee ~$850-$1,050 per home (2026) + BPUB impact fees (amount TBD)
cedar-park: Add ~$6,350 water+wastewater impact fees per home (1 LUE; ~$3,170 ww + ~$3,180 water)
arlington: In floodplain set lowest floor and finished garage 2 ft above fully urbanized BFE (not FEMA effective BFE).
austin: If in Austin regulatory floodplain (old FEMA 500-yr), lowest floor >= 100-yr WSE + 2 ft
beaumont: Require FEMA flood zone/BFE input; if in SFHA set lowest floor >= BFE + 1 ft (assumed) and elevation certificate
brownsville: If in SFHA: lowest floor >= BFE + 1 ft (assumed)
amarillo: Building permit $0.45/sf (2019 rate)
arlington: Permit by sq ft tiers (Table 2: $0.80 up to 1,200; $0.64 1,201-2,000) + 35% plan review.
austin: Plan review fee tier by sq ft ($1,141 for 2,001-3,000 sf) + 6% surcharge; other permit fees TBD
beaumont: Building permit = $0.50 x sq ft (min $55) + $150 plan review + $10 usage; MEP permits separate.
amarillo: Ask user for district (R-1/R-2/R-3) and plat setbacks; provisional R-2: front 25, side 5, rear unknown, height 35 ft
arlington: Ask for the actual zoning district (default RS-7.2) and plat building lines; no setbacks verified yet, so do not auto-fill.
cedar-park: Ask user for district (SU/SR/ES or PUD) and plat building lines; values from Zoneomics copy of UDC

celina: Ask for the lot's PD ordinance; most new Celina lots are PDs on an SF-R base. Use PD Area Regulations; if unknown use example-PD defaults front 20 / side 5 / corner side 15 / rear 20 ft and flag for confirmation.
arlington: Cap height at 40 ft in RS-7.2.
austin: Max height 35 ft (32 ft inside Subchapter F boundary)
brownsville: Max height 35 ft
cedar-park: Max height 35 ft (SU)
amarillo: Electrical per NEC 2023 (IRC Part VIII excluded)
beaumont: Use 2021 IRC/IECC and NEC 2020 for Beaumont plan notes; include ICC 600 high-wind provisions where used.
cedar-park: Use 2021 IRC (appendices AA,AB,AC,AE,AG,AH,AJ,AK,AN,AP), 2021 IECC, 2021 IPC, NEC 2020
college-station: Electrical to NEC 2023
arlington: RS-7.2 minimum lot 7,200 sf, 60 ft wide, 100 ft deep.
austin: Accept lots >= 1,800 sq ft and >= 15 ft wide for one small-lot SF home (HOME Phase 2)
brownsville: R-1 min lot 5,000 sf, 50 ft wide, 70 ft deep
college-station: GS min lot 5,000 sf, 50 ft wide, 100 ft deep
arlington: Do not apply a city masonry percentage (Gov't Code ch. 3000); prompt for HOA, deed or historic-district requirements.
beaumont: Do not apply any city-mandated masonry %; only flag HOA/deed restriction check
celina: Do not enforce city masonry %; prompt for PD/HOA masonry requirement.
dallas: Do not apply any masonry percentage by default (Gov't Code ch. 3000). Show a prompt only if the lot is in a historic district or a PD or deed restriction requires masonry.
beaumont: Read platted building lines from the recorded plat; they override district defaults when larger
cedar-park: Most new homes are in PUDs/MUDs or HOA subdivisions - plat building lines, PUD standards and deed restrictions may override district setbacks and add masonry rules
conroe: Read front/side building lines from recorded subdivision plat (Ch. 94).
forney: Read platted building lines from the recorded plat; they override district defaults when larger
celina: Check HOA/deed restrictions and platted building lines.
cypress-unincorporated-harris: Master-planned community ACC: masonry %, garage orientation, roof pitch, min house size
fort-worth: Ask for HOA/deed restrictions (often impose masonry %, minimum size, garage orientation in new Fort Worth subdivisions).
frisco: Check HOA/deed restrictions and platted building lines; typical Frisco HOAs control masonry, roof pitch, garage orientation and minimum size.

beaumont: Apply TDI windstorm package for Inland II zone: design to 143 mph Vult (ASCE 7-10 equiv. of 110 mph) - re-check under 2024 IRC/ASCE 7-22 for certifications after 1 Apr 2026; ICC 600 high-wind prescriptive option; engineer windstorm certification and WPI-8; continuous load path.

brownsville: TDI windstorm (TWIA) package: on/after Apr 1, 2026 design and build to the 2024 IRC as adopted by TDI (28 TAC 5.4013); a TDI-appointed qualified inspector or Texas PE must certify, TDI issues WPI-8 Certificate of Compliance needed for TWIA insurance. Brownsville = legacy Inland I (TDI note).
brownsville: Wind-borne debris region: all exterior glazed openings (windows, glass doors, skylights) impact-rated or protected by tested shutters/approved panels; garage doors wind-rated.

brownsville: 2024 IRC enhanced roof deck protection / sheathing attachment in wind-design-required areas (Vult >= 130 mph): spec sealed roof deck underlayment and high-wind sheathing nailing; engineer to confirm schedule.
arlington: Limit lot coverage to 50% in RS-7.2.
austin: Building coverage max 40% of lot
brownsville: Max lot coverage 50% including accessory buildings
celina: Note 20% open space requirement applies at district/subdivision level (half usable); do not apply as a per-lot coverage cap unless PD says so.
arlington: Front-facing garage: apply UDC 4.1.6.G garage setback; keep garage openings <= 55% of house width (proposed 2025).
fort-worth: Allow attached garage side setback 3 ft only if garage is >=18 ft behind front wall; detached garage behind rear wall may be 3 ft from lot line.

frisco: On front-entry (non-alley) lots apply Frisco Front Entry Lot Layout Guidelines - prefer J-swing/side-entry or recessed front garage; alley lots: rear garage 20 ft from alley (24 ft for swing-in). Treat as warning until PD/guideline values loaded.
georgetown: Provisional: set front-loaded garage door >= 25 ft from front property line / street ROW
celina: Do not add a residential sprinkler mandate (state preemption) unless city shows a pre-2009 grandfathered rule.
cypress-unincorporated-harris: No sprinklers
el-paso: Do not require residential fire sprinklers (R313 deleted locally)
frisco: If conditioned area + garage area >= 6,000 sq ft, require automatic fire sprinkler system (Frisco Fire Prevention approval) and add cost.
arlington: Assume the NCTCOG regional amendments to the 2021 IRC and IECC (Chapter 11 deleted and replaced by the IECC; carport exception) until the city ordinance is confirmed.
austin: Plumbing per UPC (IAPMO) not IPC
dallas: Use IPC 2021 (Dallas amendments) rules for fixtures and venting, not UPC.
fort-worth: Plumbing per 2021 IPC/IFGC (not UPC).

brownsville: Use basic (ultimate) design wind speed 150 mph for TDI windstorm areas under the 2024 IRC R301.2.1 (per City of Corpus Christi summary of TDI adoption); Risk Category II; exposure C, check D near open water/bays.

corpus-christi: Use basic (ultimate) design wind speed 150 mph for TDI windstorm areas under the 2024 IRC R301.2.1 (per City of Corpus Christi summary of TDI adoption); Risk Category II; exposure C, check D near open water/bays.
cypress-unincorporated-harris: Design wind ~130 mph (non-windstorm area)
el-paso: Design wind speed 115 mph (local table; 2015-era value, verify 2021 table)
austin: Impervious cover max 45% (house+garage+driveway+patios); watershed rules may be lower
cedar-park: Check TCEQ Edwards map: recharge/contributing zone homes fall under 30 TAC 213; confirm the subdivision has an approved WPAP/CZP, else individual plan needed

georgetown: Check TCEQ Edwards Aquifer map: lots on recharge zone fall under 30 TAC 213 (WPAP at subdivision level; single-family on lots > 5 ac one home exempt); city UDC Ch.13 impervious cover limits apply city+ETJ - read plat impervious cover allocation per lot
kyle: West Kyle lots may be on Edwards recharge/contributing zone: check TCEQ map; 30 TAC 213 applies to private residences unless covered by subdivision-approved plan (or lot > 5 ac, 1 home)
austin: Require tree survey input: trees >=19 in DBH protected (permit), >=24 in listed species heritage (no removal w/o variance); keep footprint out of critical root zones
cedar-park: Tree survey; heritage >= 26 in: avoid or budget $450/inch fee-in-lieu (3:1); $300/in 19-25.9 in, $150/in 8-18.9 in
conroe: Flag Ch. 102 tree/canopy rules (30% canopy standard) - capture existing trees on survey.

dallas: Ask for a tree survey (trees 6 in caliper or more within 50 ft of work). Estimate inch-for-inch replacement for protected trees outside the unrestricted zone. Plant at least three 2-in trees, two in the front yard.
cypress-unincorporated-harris: PE-designed post-tensioned slab (Houston-area expansive clay)
dallas: Default the foundation to a post-tensioned slab on grade designed for expansive clay (IRC R403.1.8 / IBC 1808.6). Add a geotech report line item.
hutto: Assume high-PI expansive clay: PT slab with geotech report; large PVR
new-braunfels: West-side lots: shallow limestone excavation adder; east-side: expansive clay
austin: Visitability: provide accessible bathroom on entry level with 30x30 in clear floor space and accessible entry
denton: Base code 2021 IRC + 2021 IECC with Denton/NCTCOG amendments; electrical NEC 2020 (verify).
houston: Check Houston-amended egress opening (R310) and exterior deck guard rules before finalising bedrooms/decks
mckinney: Use 2024 IRC / 2024 IECC / 2024 IPC-IMC-IFGC as base code for permits applied on or after 2025-10-01.
league-city: City permit set to 2021 IRC/IECC (CZ 2A); separate TDI windstorm submittal to 2024 IRC.
midland: Include ACCA Manual J (or RS summary) and energy compliance statement in permit set
sugar-land: Design to 2024 IRC + 2024 IECC (CZ 2A) + NEC 2023 with Ord. 2395 amendments for applications on/after Jan 21 2026 (not the 2021 IRC baseline).
texas-baseline: Energy compliance to 2015 IRC Chapter 11 statewide minimum unless the city adopted a newer IECC/IRC energy chapter; include REScheck/ERI documentation
conroe: No city zoning: do not apply district setbacks/height/coverage; require user to enter plat building lines and deed-restriction setbacks.
cypress-unincorporated-harris: No zoning - take setbacks from plat building lines and deed restrictions; ask for HOA design guidelines
houston: Disable district selection; use Chapter 42 building lines + plat + deed restrictions instead of zoning setbacks
texas-unincorporated: Disable zoning setbacks/height/coverage; use plat building lines and deed restrictions as setbacks
beaumont: Require Texas-registered engineer windstorm certification for the house (city rule: all buildings >= 120 sf).
corpus-christi: Windstorm plans sealed by TDI-certified windstorm engineer in permit set
houston: Require sealed truss/engineered-lumber drawings and construction-ready (non-preliminary) plan set
new-braunfels: Drawing set: sealed foundation + bracing sheets and engineer foundation letter
amarillo: Footings min 24 in below grade for any structure > 600 sf (city IRC amendment R403.1.4)
amarillo: Water service >= 12 in deep and 6 in below frost line; gas pipe >= 18 in cover
el-paso: Footing depth = max(12 in IRC R403.1.4, 6 in local frost line) = 12 in below undisturbed grade
lubbock: Frost line 12 in below grade (city criteria)
cypress-unincorporated-harris: Add MUD tap/capital fees placeholder; MUD tax affects owner cost
garland: Electric service is from Garland Power & Light (city utility), not Oncor. Use city utility connection fees once found.
hutto: Ask which water provider serves the lot (city vs WSC) - tap/impact fees differ
sugar-land: Add water connection $915 (5/8-in) + sewer tap $200.
cedar-park: Minimum living area 1,500 sf in SU
garland: For every two bedrooms provide one full bathroom and 120 sq ft of living area.
leander: Minimum living area 1,200 sf in SFU, 1,500 sf in SFS
el-paso: Set Seismic Design Category C; detached one-/two-family dwellings exempt from IRC R301.2.2 seismic provisions, but townhouse/attached products must apply SDC C seismic detailing
midland: Keep SDC A per IRC, but show advisory about induced earthquakes (M5.2 Dec 2022) - suggest crack control joints/flexible connections
texas-baseline: SDC A statewide default; check El Paso area for higher SDC
amarillo: Flag ground snow load input (Panhandle about 15-20 psf; not confirmed)
el-paso: Ground snow load 5 psf (use IRC minimum roof live load 20 psf governs)
lubbock: Ground snow load 15 psf (city Table R301.2(1))
amarillo: Default roof to Class 4 impact-resistant (recommended, not code)
lubbock: Default roof spec to Class 4 (UL 2218) impact-resistant shingles as recommended option (not code)
texas-baseline: Offer Class 4 impact-resistant roofing option (DFW, Panhandle, Central TX)
austin: Inside McMansion boundary: long side walls need an offset (articulation) - flag for review until trigger length verified
killeen: Include >= 5 listed architectural elements and >= 2 front-elevation features (corbels, quoins, louvered vents, keystones, etc.); use checklist
austin: Allow up to 3 units on SF-1/2/3 lots; FAR 0.55/3,200 (2 units) or 0.65/4,350 (3 units) inside boundary, per-unit max 0.4/2,300

dallas: Block a by-right ADU in R-7.5(A). Offer it only with a Board of Adjustment special exception or an ADU overlay, at most the greater of 700 sq ft or 25% of the main house, one story, owner-occupancy deed restriction.
austin: If inside McMansion boundary and single unit: gross floor area <= max(0.4 x lot area, 2,300 sq ft)
austin: Inside McMansion boundary: setback plane starting 15 ft above grade at side/rear lines, sloping inward 45 deg; check roof/dormers
austin: Mechanical design must include AC able to hold <=85 F and >=15 F below outdoor
college-station: Warn when plan has more than 4 bedrooms intended for unrelated occupants: max 4 unrelated per dwelling (2 in ROO). Do not market 5+ bed 'stealth dorm' layouts as rentals
college-station: Parking may scale with bedrooms (assumed; College Station ties single-family parking to bedroom count) - check before adding bedrooms
el-paso: Termite: moderate to heavy - include termite protection (R318) on drawings
fort-worth: Site plan must show lot surface drainage diverted to storm sewer conveyance (amended R401.3).
